Evidence preserved and NOT registered, in the event this file is reopened. (1) A dedicated StatPearls chapter on ulnar collateral ligament injury, titled for Gamekeeper's Thumb, which is the located source that most directly establishes the two names as one lesion. (2) A review of thumb metacarpophalangeal ulnar and radial collateral ligament injuries, which frames both conditions within a single injury category rather than as separate diseases. (3) A prospective study of complete thumb ulnar collateral ligament injury treated by surgical repair, and a long-term outcomes study of primary repair of acute injuries of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint ulnar collateral ligament, which are the located anchors for the chronic-instability and post-traumatic-degeneration routes already owned by the sibling identity. NONE of these was registered here, because the sibling identity gamekeeper-s-thumb already carries the registered rank-1 edge to osteoarthritis from batch 36 and the evidence supporting an osteoarthritis route for this lesion is the same evidence.

Not a candidate for a distinct route on present evidence. The differential between the two mechanisms is the mechanism of injury, not the disease, and a reviewing clinician who needs the mechanism should read it as a documented feature of the sibling identity rather than as a second catalog entry, exactly as the alias structure of this catalog already handles mechanism-variant conditions elsewhere.

PRESERVED-EVIDENCE RECORD COMPLETED (2026-09-28, every PMID below verified against PubMed by NCBI efetch on that date): the evidence item descriptions recorded above are prose, not verbatim titles, so each item is now resolved to a VERIFIED candidate set with the matching text or design feature stated on the record, and a future reopening of the pair needs no re-search. (1) THE DEDICATED CHAPTER TITLED FOR GAMEKEEPER'S THUMB - Mohseni M, Sina RE, Graham C. Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injury (Gamekeeper's Thumb). StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing; 2024 Feb 1. PMID 29494005. CONFIRMED as the located source that most directly establishes the two names as one lesion: the chapter states that the condition 'has also been referred to as skier's thumb since it is more commonly observed in individuals who fall while holding ski poles, which mechanistically causes the same type of hyperextension thumb injury.' (2) REVIEW(S) FRAMING BOTH NAMES INSIDE ONE THUMB ULNAR COLLATERAL LIGAMENT INJURY CATEGORY - Ritting AW, Baldwin PC, Rodner CM. Ulnar collateral ligament injury of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint. Clin J Sport Med. 2010;20(2):106-12. PMID 20215892, which treats gamekeeper's thumb (chronic, repetitive-stress attenuation) and skier's thumb (acute, valgus force on an abducted thumb) as two names for the same ligament injury inside one review; corroborated by Richard JR. Gamekeeper's thumb: ulnar collateral ligament injury. Am Fam Physician. 1996;53(5):1775-81. PMID 8623701 (one injury, once a chronic occupational injury in gamekeepers and now most frequently an acute sports injury in skiers) and by Madan SS, Pai DR, Kaur A, Dixit R. Injury to ulnar collateral ligament of thumb. Orthop Surg. 2014;6(1):1-7. PMID 24590986 (frequently described in skiers, also in rugby, soccer, handball, basketball and volleyball). (3) PROSPECTIVE STUDY OF COMPLETE THUMB ULNAR COLLATERAL LIGAMENT INJURY TREATED BY SURGICAL REPAIR - Moharram AN. Repair of thumb metacarpophalangeal joint ulnar collateral ligament injuries with microanchors. Ann Plast Surg. 2013;71(5):500-2. PMID 24126337 (prospective functional results in 27 patients after open repair, acutely or delayed up to 9 weeks, evaluated at least 16 months after surgery); Rocchi L, Merolli A, Morini A, Monteleone G, Foti C. A modified spica-splint in postoperative early-motion management of skier's thumb lesion: a randomized clinical trial. Eur J Phys Rehabil Med. 2014;50(1):49-57. PMID 24185690 (thirty consecutive patients with a diagnosis of acute complete tear of the ligament, all treated surgically, randomized prospective); and also available for the same purpose, Legerstee IWF, van der Oest MJW, Souer JS, Hundepool CA, Duraku LS, Selles RW, Zuidam JM. Patient-Reported Outcomes and Function After Surgical Repair of the Ulnar Collateral Ligament of the Thumb. J Hand Surg Am. 2023;48(8):780-787. PMID 37294237 (76 patients, complete rupture, prospectively collected outcomes). (4) LONG-TERM OUTCOMES OF PRIMARY REPAIR OF ACUTE THUMB METACARPOPHALANGEAL ULNAR COLLATERAL LIGAMENT INJURY - Picard F, Khalifa H, Dubert T. Duration of sick leave after surgical repair of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint with K-wire immobilization: prospective case series of 21 patients. Hand Surg Rehabil. 2016;35(2):122-6. PMID 27117126 (average follow-up 3 years 5 months after surgical repair of complete rupture); Samora JB, Harris JD, Griesser MJ, Ruff ME, Awan HM. Outcomes after injury to the thumb ulnar collateral ligament--a systematic review. Clin J Sport Med. 2013;23(4):247-54. PMID 23615487 (14 articles, 293 thumbs, minimum 2 years mean follow-up, 200 acute and 93 chronic injuries, osteoarthritis among the documented untreated and post-injury outcomes); and the current synthesis, Legerstee IWF, Derksen BM, van der Oest MJW, Hundepool CA, Duraku LS, Selles RW, Zuidam JM. Clinical outcomes after primary repair for thumb ulnar collateral ligament ruptures: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Hand Surg Eur Vol. 2024;49(5):534-545. PMID 38488512 (29 studies, all repair techniques and immobilization protocols yielding satisfactory outcomes). (5) THE MORPHOLOGIC ANALYSIS OF THUMB ULNAR COLLATERAL LIGAMENT AVULSION-FRACTURE FRAGMENTS named in the catalog-gap note above - Arranz Lopez J, Alzaga F, Molina J. Acute ulnar collateral ligament injuries of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint: an anatomical and clinical study. Acta Orthop Belg. 1998;64(4):378-84. PMID 9922540 (fresh-specimen anatomical and clinical study reporting avulsion fragments rotated 90 degrees in 2 of 9 avulsion-fracture cases although they appeared only slightly displaced on radiographs); Kuz JE, Husband JB, Tokar N, McPherson SA. Outcome of avulsion fractures of the ulnar base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb treated nonsurgically. J Hand Surg Am. 1999;24(2):275-82. PMID 10194010 (fragment size and rotation morphometrics in 30 patients, mean follow-up 3.1 years, 25 percent nonunion). Item (5) is recorded because the avulsion fracture of the thumb has no catalog identity; it is catalog-gap evidence, not route evidence.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 84 (2026-09-27): CLOSED as IDENTITY-DUPLICATION, following the eczema and atopic-dermatitis-eczema finding of batch 80 and the rotator-cuff-tear and rotator-cuff-injury finding of batch 82. This is the THIRD identity-duplication finding, and the THREE together now establish a recurring catalog-hygiene problem rather than coincidence: in every case the same disease is carried under two catalog names, in two of the three cases one name already holds the registered edges, and in this case the two names sit in the same catalog file with the same body system and the same applicable rating framework, which is the tightest form the problem has taken.

The evidence for duplication here is stronger than for either predecessor because the located literature itself does the merging. A dedicated review chapter is titled for one of the two names, thumb metacarpophalangeal ulnar and radial collateral ligament injuries are reviewed as a single injury category, and the distinguishing feature between skier's thumb and gamekeeper's thumb in the literature is the MECHANISM of injury, a ski pole grip producing valgus stress versus forced abduction, rather than a difference in the lesion. The sibling identity gamekeeper-s-thumb already carries the registered rank-1 edge to osteoarthritis authored in batch 36 from long-term surgical follow-up of chronic thumb ulnar collateral ligament injury, so authoring under this identity would register the same disease and the same route a second time under a different catalog name.

Deliberately reversible and deliberately NOT reconciled here. Choosing a canonical name changes the meaning of existing mappings, including which conditions point at this disease, and that is a reviewed decision for a human rather than a side effect of a citation batch. If skier-s-thumb is later elected canonical, the gamekeeper-s-thumb edge and this file must be reconciled together; the closure is recorded so the backlog filter counts it among marked deferral records and so the duplication stops generating new candidates.

Sibling check performed and reported: trigger-thumb and amputation-of-thumb-fingers-toes were examined as adjacent identities in the same body system and are GENUINELY DISTINCT, one being a stenosing flexor tendon condition at the A1 pulley and the other a digit-level amputation, so no duplication finding is recorded for either. This is the same sibling-disclosure discipline applied in the seborrheic-dermatitis and seborrheic-keratosis check in batch 82.

Catalog gap recorded without numbering: avulsion fracture of the thumb, which the located morphologic analysis of thumb ulnar collateral ligament avulsion fracture fragments addresses, has no catalog identity. It is recorded rather than numbered as a refusal because the disposition here is identity scope rather than a decision about the evidence.
